m:nieuwmarkt: By day the area is quiet and free to walk around. In the red-light district don't photograph the windows; watch out for pickpockets, especially in the evening. You pay to go inside the Oude Kerk.
m:dam: From outside it's all free. The Royal Palace and the Nieuwe Kerk can be visited inside for a fee, with hours that change for ceremonies and exhibitions: check the websites before buying.
m:spui: The Begijnhof is residential: speak quietly and don't enter the houses. The flower market is usually open every day from 9am to 5:30pm (Sundays from 11am), but it's very touristy. On Spui there's a book market on Fridays and an art market on Sundays (about 11am–6pm).
m:canali: Tickets for the Anne Frank House are only sold online, with a time slot (€16.50): they're not sold at the door. The canals are always free; watch out for bikes on the bridges.
m:jordaan: On Monday mornings (about 9am–1pm) the Noordermarkt hosts a flea market and on Saturdays (about 9am–4pm) an organic market; on other days it's a quiet square.
m:museumplein: The lawn and the tunnel are free. The Rijksmuseum (€25) and the Van Gogh (€27) can only be visited with a timed ticket, best bought online.
m:pijp: The market is open Monday to Saturday, usually from 9:30am to 5pm; on Sundays it's closed and the area is calmer. Some stalls only take cash.
m:annefrankins: Ticket €16.50 (including €1 booking fee), online only and with a time slot: not sold at the door. Every Tuesday at 10am they release visits for six weeks later, so for this trip you should look for tickets now. Usually open every day 9am–10pm.
m:rijks: Ticket €25 (free under 18), timed, best bought online. Open every day 9am–5pm, public holidays included.
m:vangogh: Ticket about €27, timed and online only. Usual hours are 9am–5pm, with evening openings on some days: check the website before buying (I couldn't see the official page).
m:jodenbuurt: The Waterlooplein market is usually open Monday to Saturday, 9:30am to 6pm. Museums and gardens have their own tickets: choose based on your time.
m:vondel: The park is free and always open. Foodhallen (Hannie Dankbaarpassage 16) is open every day from noon to 11pm: each stall sets its own prices.
m:noord: The ferries are free and leave every few minutes for pedestrians and cyclists; for the former NDSM industrial area take line F4 (about 15 minutes). The EYE building and its terrace are free, exhibitions and films are paid.
vd:pancake: A tiny first-floor room with four tables and a steep staircase: large, thin Dutch pancakes, sweet or savoury, made to order. Cash only.
vp:pancake: A pancake usually costs €9–13 (menu not seen): bring cash.
vd:vleminckx: A historic little stand: double-fried Dutch chips, eaten standing up, with your choice of sauce (sauces cost extra). There's almost always a queue, but it moves fast.
vp:vleminckx: A small cone costs around €5 and a large one about €7–8, sauces excluded (menu not seen).
vd:frens: The herring cart: the «broodje haring» (a bun with raw herring, onion and pickles) is the ultimate Dutch fast food. Next to the flower market, eaten standing on the bridge.
vp:frens: A herring sandwich usually costs €4–6. Opening hours vary between sources: best to go around midday.
vd:winkel43: The Noordermarkt café-bar that makes the city's most famous apple pie: thick, with cinnamon and whipped cream. Outdoor tables on the square and simple breakfasts until 3pm.
vp:winkel43: Breakfast around €6–10; apple pie with coffee is under €10 (menu not seen).
vd:vlaamsch: An artisan bakery with sourdough bread, croissants and filled rolls, on one of the liveliest shopping streets in the centre. Take away or eat at the few tables.
vp:vlaamsch: A sandwich or a croissant with coffee stays under €8 (menu not seen).
vd:petit: A French pâtisserie on Haarlemmerstraat: tartlets, éclairs, macarons and cakes, to take away or eat at the little tables. Open Tuesday to Saturday.
vp:petit: A pastry with coffee is under €9 (menu not seen).
vd:holtkamp: A traditional pâtisserie with a glass-and-brass window and famous croquettes and cakes: the classic snack before or after the museums. Closed on Sundays.
vp:holtkamp: A pastry with coffee is under €9 (menu not seen).
vd:backblack: Specialty coffee a short walk from Museumplein: filter coffee, cakes and simple sandwiches, with outdoor tables when the sun's out.
vp:backblack: Coffee and a cake stay under €9 (menu not seen).
vd:scandi: De Pijp's Nordic café, next to Sarphatipark: excellent filter coffee, cinnamon buns and Scandinavian open sandwiches, in a bright room.
vd:rudis: The stroopwafel shop at the market: Dutch waffles with caramel syrup made fresh, warm and soft. The ideal snack while you walk around the market.
vp:rudis: A warm stroopwafel usually costs €3–4 (menu not seen).
vd:spang: Neighbourhood Surinamese and Indonesian cooking: roti with chicken, nasi and satay, in a simple room in De Pijp. One of the cheapest dinners in the area.
vp:spang: A dish usually costs €11–15 (menu not seen). The hours shown are Monday's: check the other days.
vd:stubbe: The herring cart closest to Central Station, on the bridge over the Singel: raw herring, herring sandwiches and kibbeling. Eaten standing up, cash only.
vp:stubbe: A sandwich costs about €5.50. Sources give different hours: best to go around midday, with cash.
vd:bird: The Zeedijk Thai restaurant that started as a snack bar: curries, noodles and satay in a small, noisy room. Next door, its snack bar opens from 5 to 11pm.
vp:bird: The cheapest dishes start from €10; mains reach €20–25 (menu not seen).
vd:foodhallen: The indoor market in a former tram depot in Oud-West: 19 stalls with ramen, pizza, bao, dim sum, tacos, sandwiches and desserts. Everyone orders where they like and you eat together at long tables.
vp:foodhallen: A dish from a stall usually costs €8–14, bitterballen included (each stall sets its own prices).
cd:stedelijk: Modern and contemporary art and design: Mondrian, Malevich and Warhol.
cd:rembrandthuis: The house where Rembrandt lived and worked, with his studio and his etchings.
cd:heineken: The old brewery: an interactive tour with tastings.
cd:scheepvaart: The maritime museum, in the old naval arsenal, with a replica of a Golden Age ship.
cd:moco: Banksy, Warhol and Kusama in a villa near Museumplein.
cd:adam: The tower on the IJ, a few minutes by free ferry from Central Station: city views and a swing over the edge.
cd:canalcruise: An hour on the central canals with commentary: bridges, houseboats and merchants' houses.
cd:nemo: The ship-shaped science museum, with hands-on experiments and a rooftop terrace.
